notes:
Connecticut imposes no franchise-type tax on a default LLC. The Corporation Business Tax (ch. 208) is the state's franchise tax, but its subjects are "companies" as defined in section 12-213 - corporations, joint stock companies and associations - and its imposition reaches only entities acting "in a corporate capacity or as an unincorporated association taxable as a corporation for federal income tax purposes". A default LLC is neither. The Unincorporated Business Tax (ch. 228) was repealed for income years beginning on or after 1983. The only entity-level tax chapter naming an LLC is ch. 228z, the Affected Business Entity Tax, and it is an elective income tax: section 12-699(b) lets an affected business entity elect to pay 6.99 per cent of a Connecticut-source income base, and members then credit 87.5 per cent of the entity-level tax against their own income tax. That is the pass-through entity tax election, not a levy on being registered, so applies is false and hasPTETElection is true.
stateIncomeTax: the income tax is imposed on "each resident of this state", and section 12-699(f) treats members of affected business entities as the persons subject to chapter 229, which is the pass-through posture. The top rate is 6.99 per cent for taxable years commencing on or after January 1, 2024, at $500,000 / $800,000 / $1,000,000 thresholds depending on filing status; the flat trust-and-estate rate is the same 6.99 per cent.
collectedWithAnnualReport is null by construction: with no franchise-type levy there is no overlap with root states.json's annual_report_fee (80 for Connecticut, the Secretary of State's annual report filing).
